item.title: Cynomolgus Monkey (Macaca fascicularis) Embryo Models: From Developmental Benchmarks to Functionally Testable Embryoids
item.description: Stem cell-based embryo models now reconstruct increasingly advanced stages of mammalian development, but developmental fidelity remains a central limitation. This review examines why cynomolgus monkey systems are biologically necessary, how natural embryos and emerging technologies benchmark primate development, and how advanced monkey embryoids can strengthen interpretation of human embryo models.

item.title: Synergistic Charge Scavenging in Pt/C-Polyoxometalate Systems for Scalable Biomass Power Generation via Super-Reduced Electrolytes
item.description: Direct electrochemical conversion of unrefined biomass waste into electricity offers a sustainable pathway for decentralized energy generation, yet its practical implementation has been fundamentally hindered by low power densities and limited scalability. A fundamental bottleneck lies in the intrinsic recalcitrance of biomass, which restricts electron harvesting to shallow oxidation pathways and confines redox mediators to low reduction states. Here, we demonstrate a scalable biomass flow fuel...

item.title: Encapsulated mitochondrial transplantation: Advancing organelle therapeutics
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Entrainment of prefrontal theta synchrony increases interbrain coupling and enhances social interaction in mouse models of autism
item.description: Social interaction requires the integration of information about self, other, and shared context. One of the proposed mechanisms supporting this coordination is interbrain synchrony - correlated neural activity between interacting individuals - yet its role in shaping social behavior remains unresolved. Here, we show that theta band synchrony in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) is closely linked to social interaction in mice and often precedes its onset. In male Shank2 mutant mice, a genetic...

item.title: Long-term oncological outcomes of robotic versus laparoscopic total mesorectal excision for rectal cancer: COLRAR randomized clinical trial
item.description: CONCLUSION: R-TME and L-TME produced equivalent 5-year oncological outcomes. A post-hoc analysis suggested improved local control with robotic surgery after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, requiring confirmation in prospectively designed studies.

item.title: Low-dose CT denoising using a diffusion prior via score distillation sampling
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The results show that diffusion-based image priors can be leveraged across various low-dose levels within the proposed optimization-based denoising framework. Our work suggests that SDS-guided diffusion priors are a promising direction for LDCT denoising in data-limited settings.

item.title: Twelve-Month Efficacy and Tolerability of Netarsudil 0.02% in Korean Patients with Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma and Normal-Tension Glaucoma: A Single-Center Retrospective Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: In eyes already receiving ocular hypotensive therapy (mean baseline IOP 17.3 mmHg, over a third with NTG), adding or substituting netarsudil lowered IOP by a further 3 mmHg, sustained to 12 months in eyes continuing it. Discontinuation reflected tolerability, not loss of effect: a third stopped within a year, almost always from ocular surface symptoms - close to the registration programme but above other real-world reports.

item.title: Participatory Epidemiology of Major Camel Diseases and Their Management in Somalia: The Case of Banadir and Lower Shabelle Regions
item.description: This study investigates major camel diseases, their community-perceived epidemiological characteristics, and management practices in the Banadir and Lower Shabelle regions of Somalia. Data were collected from 17 key informants through semistructured interviews and from 18 participants across three focus group discussions (FGDs). Semistructured interviews captured key camel diseases, their local names, disease impacts, coping mechanisms, and locally used disease management approaches, while FGDs...

item.title: LncRNA FLJ20021 Restrains Fibroblast Senescence and Matrix Remodeling in Pelvic Organ Prolapse by Promoting XRCC6-Dependent ADI1 Transcription
item.description: Pelvic-organ prolapse (POP) is an age-associated disorder that is often accompanied by uterosacral ligament (USL) weakening and extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation; however, the upstream regulators linking fibroblast aging to ECM remodeling remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify an uncharacterized long non-coding RNA (lncRNA), FLJ20021, as significantly downregulated in POP-derived USL tissues and primary human uterosacral-ligament fibroblasts (hUSLFs) compared with non-POP controls....

item.title: Blood transcriptomic signatures of vascular risk in Alzheimer's disease
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Lifestyle and environmental factors contributing to cardiovascular risk are components of the exposome, yet molecular signatures associated with cumulative cardiovascular risk in Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain incompletely understood.

item.title: Preoperative Muscle Mass and 1-Year Diabetes Remission After Metabolic Surgery: Associations Across Remission Definitions
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative muscle mass was not associated with consensus-defined diabetes remission but was associated with stringent biochemical normoglycaemia after metabolic surgery. Adding either absolute TMM or RMM to established remission scores improved cross-validated discrimination for this stringent outcome; however, these findings remain exploratory and require external validation.

item.title: Improving Haemorrhage Prediction in General Ward Patients by Incorporating Patterns of Change Derived From Routine Ward Measurements
item.description: CONCLUSION: Patterns of change derived from routine ward measurements provided complementary predictive information for haemorrhage prediction in general ward patients beyond the most recent clinical measurements. Routinely collected ward data may therefore contain additional predictive information not captured by the most recent values alone.

item.title: A stealth-body Fc engineering platform enables complete effector silencing in antibody and ADC therapeutics
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, SB Fc variants represent a generalizable, effector-null Fc scaffold that enables complete and transferable silencing of Fc-mediated immune functions while preserving key developability attributes. This platform expands the therapeutic window of antibody therapeutics through precise control of Fc activity across diverse modalities.

item.title: Spatiotemporally resolved single-nucleus transcriptomics reveals cellular and regional vulnerability in the midbrain in Parkinson's disease
item.description: Parkinson's disease (PD) is clinically and biologically heterogeneous, and ethnic differences may influence its pathogenesis. However, single-nucleus transcriptomic data from East Asian populations remain limited. Here, we present a spatially resolved single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas of the human substantia nigra (SN) across the PD continuum, control, incidental Lewy body disease (iLBD), and advanced PD, in pathologically confirmed Korean individuals. Our integrative analysis revealed early...

item.title: Azithromycin versus ceftriaxone for uncomplicated typhoid fever in children: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
item.description: CONCLUSION: Azithromycin appears to have comparable efficacy and safety to ceftriaxone for the treatment of uncomplicated typhoid fever in children, with a trend toward fewer relapses that warrants cautious interpretation. Its oral administration may provide a practical alternative to parenteral ceftriaxone in endemic settings. Further large-scale randomized trials with standardized outcome reporting are needed to strengthen the current evidence base.

item.title: Healthcare and cost burdens associated with potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults: a matched cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSION: PIM use was associated with an increased risk of hospitalization and ED visits, as well as higher healthcare costs. These findings highlight the importance of regular medication review and optimization of prescribing in older adults. However, PIM use should be considered within the broader context of multimorbidity and frailty, rather than as an isolated risk factor, when developing strategies to improve health outcomes in this population.

item.title: Jamming-controlled stochasticity in metal-insulator switching
item.description: Understanding and controlling phase transitions is fundamental to physics and central to many technological revolutions. There is currently strong interest in materials with coupled structural and electronic phase transitions, where controlling the transition plasticity naturally yields built-in memory, key for emulating neurons and synapses in neuromorphic technologies. Here, operando coherent Bragg X-ray diffraction is used to study the evolution of the nano-domain distribution at the...

item.title: Emergent Molecular Weaving in an Ionic Metal-Organic Network for CO<sub>2</sub> Conversion
item.description: Molecular weaving has emerged as a powerful design strategy in supramolecular chemistry, yet most woven frameworks rely on rigid ligands and elaborate templating. Here, we report a minimalistic, aqueous-phase synthesis of a woven metal-organic superstructure assembled from Cu^(2+) and 2,4,6-trinitrobenzene-1,3,5-triol (TNPG). In the crystal, asymmetric coordination of TNPG with Cu^(2+) yields charged one-dimensional (1D) polymeric strands featuring both distorted octahedral and square planar...

item.title: Endohepatology in the Management of Portal Hypertension in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease
item.description: Portal hypertension is the principal driver of decompensation in advanced chronic liver disease, yet in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) it deviates from the classical sinusoidal paradigm. Growing evidence points to a mixed sinusoidal-presinusoidal phenotype in which the hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) may underestimate true portal pressure, and in which decompensation and varices can occur at lower HVPG values than in viral cirrhosis. This biology is...

item.title: Leveraging Diversity in Environmental Driven Responses Reveals a Key Role for Mesophyll Conductance and Root Sink Strength Under Elevated CO<sub>2</sub> and Temperature
item.description: In future climates both CO(2) and temperature are predicted to rise. Using high-throughput phenotyping, the diversity of 31 different banana varieties and their associated traits were leveraged to understand the impact of potential future climatic conditions of combined elevated CO(2) (e[CO(2)]) and temperature. Under ambient CO(2) (a[CO(2)]) the adaxial/abaxial stomatal density ratio (rSD) was identified as a strong predictor of growth, but its importance diminished when CO(2) was highly...

item.title: Epidemiology of Irritable Bowel Syndrome Among Chilean Adults: Differences Across Healthcare Settings and Urban-Rural Populations
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: IBS symptoms compatible with Rome IV criteria were common across the evaluated Chilean adult populations, with differences observed according to healthcare setting and sex. Although IBS prevalence did not differ significantly between the urban and rural/Mapuche populations, this finding should be interpreted cautiously given differences in age and recruitment methods. Larger population-based studies are needed to confirm these findings in rural and Indigenous populations. These data...

item.title: AZUR-4, a Phase 2, Open Label, Randomized Study of Neoadjuvant Dostarlimab Plus CAPEOX Versus CAPEOX in Previously Untreated T4N0 or Stage III Mismatch Repair Proficient/Microsatellite Stable Resectable Colon Cancer
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: AZUR-4 will evaluate the effect of neoadjuvant dostarlimab + CAPEOX in patients with previously untreated T4N0 or stage III pMMR/MSS resectable colon cancer, a population for whom improved treatments are urgently needed. The robust sampling and advanced analysis of pretreatment and posttreatment blood, tissue, and tumor samples planned for this trial should assist in elucidating immune profile analyses to support the discovery of novel predictive biomarkers in this population.

item.title: Baseline Clearance and Early Troughs Identify Candidates for Early Therapeutic Drug Monitoring During Infliximab Induction in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: A pragmatic, risk-stratified, model-informed approach centered on baseline clearance and early troughs may guide personalized infliximab induction in ulcerative colitis. External validation is warranted.

item.title: Synthesis of Nitrogen-Containing Heterocyclic Scaffolds and Applications in Scaffold Hopping: Development of an Aripiprazole Analog
item.description: Heteroaromatic ring systems play a crucial role in drug development because they modulate physicochemical properties and expand the range of molecular interactions compared to non-heterocyclic aromatic rings. They are also widely represented among approved drugs. Among heteroatoms, nitrogen is the most prevalent in the diverse scaffold space of heterocyclic drugs, including those generated by fragment-based drug discovery approach. In this work, we show the synthesis of a set of novel or...

item.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of the eHealth-faciLitated SMILe-integrated care model on treatment burden, quality of life and graft-versus-host disease after allogeneic stem cell transplantation: results of two European randomized controlled implementation studies
item.description: The SMILe Integrated Care Model (SMILe-ICM) has previously demonstrated feasibility, successful implementation, and promising effects on survival, re-hospitalization, and cost-effectiveness following allogeneic stem cell transplantation (alloSCT). To complement these findings and provide a more comprehensive evaluation of the intervention's effects, we evaluated patient-reported and clinical secondary outcomes from two RCTs. Data from two hybrid effectiveness-implementation RCTs conducted at two...

item.title: Sequential emergence of FLT3-ITD and BCR::ABL1 during disease progression in relapsed acute myeloid leukemia
item.description: Emergence of BCR::ABL1 during FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3) inhibitor therapy is a rare resistance mechanism in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). We report a case of relapsed AML with sequential clonal evolution after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT). A previously healthy man in his 30s was diagnosed with AML with maturation; initial cytogenetics were normal, and both FLT3-internal tandem duplication (FLT3-ITD) and BCR::ABL1 were absent, while targeted sequencing...

item.title: Simultaneous X-chromosome inactivation and tissue-/cell-type-specific DNA methylation in the transcriptional regulatory region of the X-linked recessive disease gene OTC
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Accordingly, by demonstrating that hypomethylated allele frequency reflects the active X allele, this study provides possible molecular evidence of skewed X inactivation through DNA methylation within the OTC T-DMR.

item.title: Long-term donor and graft safety despite subclinical mitochondrial abnormalities: mechanistic insights from a 22-year follow-up of a carrier-to-MELAS kidney transplant
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This case represents the longest reported follow-up of a living kidney transplant from an m.3243 A > G carrier. It demonstrates that maternal carriers with extremely low heteroplasmy and no light microscopic evidence of overt renal damage on biopsy can be safe donors and provide excellent long-term graft outcomes. Precise risk stratification based on genotype and biopsy findings, rather than uniform exclusion, may expand transplant options.

item.title: As Natural as Sleep: A Literature Study of Catholic Perspectives on Palliative Sedation
item.description: The Roman Catholic Church has a long-standing tradition of participating in the debates on the ethics of medical care. At the heart of the Church's reflections on this subject lies a deep respect for the dignity of individual patients and human life in general. This respect is also an expression of reverence for God and an acknowledgement of His sovereignty over human life. In the context of palliative care, these basic convictions have led to a strong rejection within Catholicism of those...

item.title: Multidisciplinary Sarcopenia Care During Chemotherapy: A Quality Improvement Project
item.description: CONCLUSION: A nurse practitioner-coordinated multidisciplinary sarcopenia care pathway can be successfully integrated into routine oncology care and may improve nursing care quality.

item.title: Scanless Centimeter-Scale Microstereolithography Enabled by Source-Plane Angular Conditioning
item.description: Achieving centimeter-scale scanless microstereolithography remains challenging in conventional projection microstereolithography (PµSL), where improving resolution inevitably restricts printable area due to the finite number of pixels. High-pixel-density LCD modulators provide a promising pathway to relax this limitation, but their large emission area introduces severe optical coupling and illumination nonuniformity in reduction projection systems. Here, we introduce source-plane angular...

item.title: Novel chemogenetic approaches in modulating calcium signaling
item.description: Calcium (Ca2+) signals regulate diverse processes ranging from neurotransmission and muscle contraction to gene expression, immune response, and cell death. Conventional pharmacological agents are readily applied but often lack molecular and cell-type specificity, whereas genetic perturbations offer greater precision but are typically slow and difficult to reverse. Chemogenetic systems bridge these approaches by combining genetically encoded protein actuators with exogenous chemical ligands. The...

item.title: Ward Failure After Severe Rib Fracture: What Unplanned ICU Transfer Teaches Us About Early Risk Stratification
item.description: BackgroundSevere rib fractures are a major cause of morbidity and mortality after blunt thoracic trauma. The decision to directly admit these patients to the intensive care unit (ICU) vs initial ward placement remains debated. An unplanned ICU transfer may reflect delayed recognition of deterioration and worsen outcomes.MethodsAdult patients (≥18 years) with isolated severe thoracic injury (thorax AIS ≥3, AIS ≤1 in all other body regions) due to blunt trauma that resulted in one or more rib...

item.title: Germicidal ultraviolet to reduce transmission of respiratory infections indoors: a systematic review
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Several older clinical studies indicated that GUV reduces infections with high transmissibility through air, but its broader effectiveness against respiratory infection remains uncertain. Inconclusive results may reflect methodological and epidemiological limitations rather than true ineffectiveness. Adequately powered RCTs with robust clinical endpoints are needed.

item.title: Preclinical modeling of trastuzumab deruxtecan in a mouse model of brain metastatic triple-negative breast cancer identifies two contributors to efficacy
item.description: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) has demonstrated clinical efficacy in advanced HER2-low to -ultralow breast cancer. We employed a mouse model of triple-negative breast cancer in the difficult-to-treat brain metastasis setting to determine T-DXd efficacy and investigate mechanism(s). T-DXd (10 and 3 mg/kg) was compared to an identical ADC except HER2-nonbinding (control) in a hematogenous model of HER2-ultralow brain-tropic triple-negative breast cancer, MDA-MB-231-BR7 (231-BR). The roles of HER2...

item.title: Tropospheric Ozone Assessment Report II: Changing health impacts of global ozone exposure
item.description: As part of the second Tropospheric Ozone Assessment Report (TOAR-II), we synthesize global observations and observationally constrained estimates of surface-level ozone (O3) with contemporary literature to characterize the global distribution and trends of long-term O3 exposure, focusing on two health-relevant metrics and health impacts attributable to long-term exposure. The highest 2016-2020 surface-level O3 concentrations are observed or estimated in South Asia, eastern China, and parts of...

item.title: Tropospheric Ozone Assessment Report II: South America regional analysis
item.description: This study presents the first regional assessment of tropospheric ozone over South America for the early twenty-first century. We use observations from 14 combined satellite records, two atmospheric reanalyses, and model simulations to examine the spatial distribution, source contributions and trends in ozone and its precursors. Satellites and reanalysis data reveal enhanced tropospheric column ozone over the mid-latitudes of the west coast and the subtropical east coast, with 2005-2021 median...

item.title: 3D Ordered Macroporous Cu-Based Multimetallic Alloy Enables Efficient Asymmetric C-C Coupling for Selective CO<sub>2</sub> Electroreduction to Ethylene
item.description: The abundant Cu⁰/Cu^(δ+) interfaces generated after reconstruction are crucial for promoting the coupling of *CO and *COH intermediates in electrocatalytic CO(2) reduction. However, Cu sites derived from a single metal severely restrict C-C coupling efficiency and product selectivity. Here, the direct regulation of the interfacial microenvironment is reported by constructing a 3D ordered macroporous (3DOM) architecture composed of multimetallic alloy (MMA) on the surface of CuO(x). The designed...

item.description: No abstract

item.title: A Systematic Review of The Role of Probiotics and Synbiotics on Semen Quality and Sperm Function in Male Infertility
item.description: CONCLUSION: The available evidence suggests that supplementation with probiotics and synbiotics holds promise for enhancing semen quality. However, the field is limited by small, heterogeneous study populations and short follow-up periods, necessitating larger, well-designed randomized controlled trials (RCTs).

item.description: No abstract

item.title: Anti-Poisoning Tin Single-Atom Unlocks High-Activity Ruthenium Catalysts for Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
item.description: The practical deployment of anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) is constrained by the lack of efficient electrocatalysts for the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), primarily due tothe sluggishVolmer step and inefficient intermediate desorption. While Ru-based catalysts exhibit promising *H binding energy, their practical performance is compromised by poor water dissociation kinetics and susceptibility to active-site blockage by adsorbed species. item.title: Autophagy-Controlled Collagen I Metabolism and ECM Homeostasis: From Molecular Mechanisms to Fibrotic Dysregulation and Therapy
item.description: Fibrotic diseases are characterized by persistent extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and excessive accumulation of fibrillar collagens, particularly Type I collagen (Col I), which collectively drive tissue stiffening, architectural distortion, and progressive organ dysfunction. However, pathological Col I dysregulation is not limited to overproduction or deposition; it may also involve defective folding, impaired trafficking, abnormal secretion, insufficient degradation, or altered collagen...

item.title: Prenatal Presentation of RMRP-Related Skeletal Dysplasia: Clinical and Genomic Expansion
item.description: The RNA subunit of the mitochondrial RNA processing endoribonuclease complex is encoded by RMRP. Biallelic variants in RMRP are known for anauxetic dysplasia 1 (AD), cartilage-hair hypoplasia (CHH), and metaphyseal dysplasia without hypotrichosis. More than 140 variants in RMRP have been reported in patients with RMRP-related disorders. Genotype-phenotype correlation is poorly understood. Patients documented are predominantly children and young adults, and prenatal onset of clinical symptoms has...

item.title: Jasmonate-Induced Metabolic Reprogramming Enhances Fruit Quality, Bioactive Compounds, and Stress Tolerance
item.description: Jasmonates (JAs), including jasmonic acid (JA), methyl jasmonate (MeJA), jasmonoyl-isoleucine (JA-Ile), and cis-jasmone, have emerged as central integrators of plant stress adaptation, developmental regulation, and fruit quality formation in horticultural crops. This review comprehensively summarizes recent advances in JA biosynthesis, metabolic conversion, signal perception, and downstream regulatory networks governing abiotic stress resilience and quality-associated traits. We highlight the...

item.title: Persistent Cholelithiasis Following Biochemical Resolution of Parenteral Nutrition-Associated Cholestasis in a Former Preterm Infant: Surgical Management With Open Cholecystectomy
item.description: Gallstones in early infancy are increasingly detected in survivors of neonatal intensive care, and most contemporary series favor observation because spontaneous resolution is common. Less well described is the divergence that may follow: cholestasis resolves completely while the stones formed during it remain. We present the case of a male infant born at 35 weeks of gestation who required high-frequency oscillatory ventilation, five vasoactive agents for septic shock, and 23 days of parenteral...

item.title: Extracellular vesicles in colorectal cancer: M2 polarization, bidirectional regulation of CAFs, metastasis, and treatment
item.description: Extracellular vesicles (EVs), as key mediators of intercellular communication, play a critical regulatory role in the pathogenesis and treatment of colorectal cancer (CRC). By carrying diverse bioactive molecules-including miRNAs, lncRNAs, circRNAs, and DNA-EVs influence multiple components of the tumor microenvironment (TME), such as promoting macrophage M2 polarization, reducing T and B Cell activity and proliferation, enabling evasion of natural killer (NK) cell surveillance, and regulating...

item.title: Global trends and hotspots of genetic research on non-syndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate: a bibliometric and bioinformatics analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study clarified the publication trends, key research forces, disciplinary distributions, and hotspots in NSCL/P genetics, revealing an ongoing shift in research focus. In silico network analyses of public databases identified distinct molecular pathways mediating alcohol- and nicotine-induced developmental disorders. These findings provide reliable evidence for future mechanistic exploration of NSCL/P pathogenesis.

item.title: A handheld polarized hyperspectral imaging probe for tissue differentiation using spectral and polarization characteristics
item.description: Polarized hyperspectral imaging (PHSI) integrates spectral and polarization contrast to enable comprehensive tissue characterization. In this study, we validate a refined handheld PHSI probe that is more compact, lightweight, and capable of rapid image acquisition. The system was evaluated on freshly excised tissues from five male mice, focusing on four organ types-brain, tongue, thyroid, and testicle-chosen for their similar macroscopic appearance but distinct biochemical and microstructural...

item.title: Automated Retinal Segmentation of Hyperspectral Images Using a Modified U-Net with Spectral Multi-head Attention
item.description: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) can capture spatial and spectral data of the retina. Retinal vessel segmentation enables quantitative analysis and assessment of retinal health. In this work, we developed an HSI system for mouse retina and a deep learning architecture to segment retinal vessels. Retinal images were manually segmented to establish ground truth. We proposed the use of multi-head attention block for the spectral data, as well as Tversky loss for segmentation refinement. The model's...

item.title: Bone quality deterioration is accompanied by mesenchymal stem cell defects in osteoporosis patients undergoing spinal fusion
item.description: As the elderly population grows, the number of osteoporosis (OP) patients undergoing spinal fusion has been increasing, and they often require more postoperative revision. Our research aims to examine the health status of autologous bone grafts and bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) in patients with OP, in order to prevent postoperative complications. Cancellous bone specimens from spinous processes were obtained from 54 aging patients (OP and non-OP groups, n = 27 for each) during...

item.title: An exploratory comparison of region-specific feather microstructure in two Eurasian tree sparrow populations across altitudes
item.description: High-altitude environments impose simultaneous challenges to avian flight and thermoregulation, potentially shaping variation in feather microstructure. We conducted an exploratory comparison of feather microstructural traits across feather regions, sexes, and altitudinal populations in the Eurasian tree sparrow (Passer montanus). Using scanning electron microscopy, we quantified vane- and downy- feather traits, including barbule length and density, hamuli number, cilia number, ventral teeth...

item.title: Prognosis and Safety of Neoadjuvant Therapy Plus Surgery versus Upfront Surgery in Patients with Resectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma at CNLC Ib-IIa Stage: A Propensity Score Matching Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative neoadjuvant therapy improves prognosis with acceptable safety in patients with resectable CNLC stage Ib-IIa HCC. In patients with SD/PR after a short course of neoadjuvant therapy, the extended strategy was associated with improved RFS compared with the short-course strategy.

item.title: Analysis of Risk Factors and Development of a Predictive Model for 1-Year Mortality After Acute Hip Fracture Surgery in Patients Aged ≥80 Years: The Prognostic Nutritional Index as a Potential Predictor
item.description: CONCLUSION: This internally validated nomogram integrating PNI and other risk factors predicts 1-year postoperative mortality in patients aged ≥80 years with hip fracture and may support clinical risk-stratification decisions.

item.title: Primary Biliary Cholangitis Diagnosed During Follow-Up of a Man with HIV Infection and Syphilis: A Case Report
item.description: CONCLUSION: In HIV-infected patients with active syphilis and liver dysfunction, abnormalities should not be attributed to infection alone. Syphilis-associated liver injury in this case remained presumptive. Recognition of PBC during immune recovery after ART suggests a possible association, not proof of causation by syphilis or immune reconstitution. Dynamic follow-up, autoantibody monitoring, and repeat liver biopsy when clinically indicated may help identify coexisting autoimmune liver...

item.title: Geophagy During Pregnancy in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Review of Cultural Practices and Health Implications
item.description: Geophagy, the intentional consumption of soil and other earth materials, is a common practice among pregnant women in many parts of sub-Saharan Africa. This narrative review aimed to examine the cultural drivers, nutritional implications and health consequences of geophagy during pregnancy, as well as identify potential intervention strategies for mitigating associated risks. Literature retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect and Google Scholar was synthesized to examine...

item.title: Validation of a polarized hyperspectral imaging (PHSI) probe using phantoms and biological tissues
item.description: Polarized hyperspectral imaging (PHSI) combines wavelength-resolved reflectance with polarization sensitivity to probe tissue absorption, scattering, and microstructural organization in a label-free manner. We developed a compact handheld PHSI probe that integrates two liquid crystal variable retarders (LCVRs), a linear polarizer, and a hyperspectral snapshot camera to achieve full Stokes imaging over the range of 460-600 nm. In this work, we establish a comprehensive calibration and validation...

item.title: Preclinical evaluation of a live attenuated bivalent Trichophyton vaccine for prophylaxis and post-infection treatment of dermatophytosis in rabbits
item.description: CONCLUSION: The live attenuated bivalent vaccine candidate demonstrated promising prophylactic activity against experimental dermatophytosis in rabbits. Post-infection clinical improvement provides preliminary evidence warranting further investigation but cannot establish therapeutic efficacy. Controlled studies in the target host should incorporate adequate comparator groups, standardized lesion scoring, quantitative and species-specific mycology, immunological endpoints, and comprehensive...

item.title: Sarcopenia and Sarcopenic Obesity in Postmenopausal Women: Limitations of BMI as a Predictor of Sarcopenic Obesity
item.description: CONCLUSION: Sarcopenia and sarcopenic obesity were prevalent among community-dwelling postmenopausal women, with lower body mass index identified as a significant predictor of both conditions. The observation that low body mass index predicts both sarcopenia and sarcopenic obesity highlights the limitations of body mass index as a measure of adiposity when assessing sarcopenic obesity in postmenopausal women.

item.title: Hyperspectral imaging of human prostate tissue with automatic segmentation and histologic validation
item.description: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is an emerging modality that captures rich spatial and spectral information, offering promise for tissue characterization and disease diagnosis. In the context of the prostate, where histopathological assessment remains the gold standard, current imaging techniques often lack sufficient ability to support fine-grained tissue discrimination. Moreover, large annotated HSI datasets are scarce due to the complexity of expert labeling, limiting the development of...

item.title: Relationship Between Dominant Follicle Diameter on the hCG Trigger Day and Live Birth After Modified Natural Cycle Frozen Embryo Transfer: A Retrospective Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Dominant follicular diameter on the hCG day was not independently associated with the live birth rate in mNC-FET. The crude difference seen in women aged advanced-age women (≥35 yeaadjustment and should be viewed as hypothesis-generating rather than effect modification. Flexible triggering may be acceptable, while maternal age remains a key clinical consideration in individualizing trigger timing.

item.title: gTranslate: rapid and accurate translation table prediction for prokaryotic genomes
item.description: BACKGROUND: Bioinformatic tools often require the prediction of protein-coding genes to make inferences about prokaryotic genomes. Typically, the genetic code used for translating genes to proteins must be specified by the user based on the taxonomic classification of a genome assembly or, for some widely used tools, established using a heuristic rule based on gene coding densities. Manual specification is at best inconvenient, but more challenging is that many bioinformatic tools are applied...

item.title: Negative impact of single housing on chronic kidney disease mineral and bone disorder outcomes
item.description: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a disorder of acquired disrupted mineral metabolism that affects millions in the United States and has no cure. Due to disturbed mineral homeostasis bones are particularly affected showing substantial bone loss during CKD and intricately linked with morbidity and mortality. Animal models serve as a crucial platform to investigate and elucidate the tissue cross-communication that facilitates pathogenic changes during CKD. One preclinical rodent model gaining in...

item.title: Impact of Dupilumab Therapy on Skin Barrier Function in Patients With Moderate-to-Severe Atopic Dermatitis: A Phase IV, Non-Randomized, Open-Label, Parallel-Group Clinical Study
item.description: Dupilumab improves skin barrier function in patients with atopic dermatitis (AD), but data for Chinese patients are limited. This 16-week, prospective, exploratory study investigated the impact of dupilumab on skin barrier function in Chinese patients with moderate-to-severe AD. Forty-four participants (24 patients with AD and 20 healthy volunteers) were enrolled. Patients with AD received dupilumab treatment every 2 weeks and were followed up to Week 16. Tape-stripped stratum corneum samples...

item.title: Assessing the construct validity of cross-national harmonized cognitive assessments using age
item.description: Harmonized cognitive measures are key to cross-national comparisons of dementia risk. However, validating such measures cross-nationally is challenging due to differences in cognitive measures and a lack of a reference standard. Age, a characteristic strongly associated with cognition and widely measured, can serve as a benchmark for evaluating how well harmonized cognitive measures are broadly compatible with a common construct. We used cross-nationally harmonized measures from three studies in...

item.title: Rhizospheric Bacteria From Artocarpus heterophyllus Exhibit Antimicrobial Traits and Antagonistic Activity Against Pantoea stewartii subsp. stewartii, Causal Agent of Jackfruit Bronzing Disease
item.description: The Jackfruit bronzing disease represents a significant phytosanitary constraint affecting Artocarpus heterophyllus production. In this context, the exploration of plant-associated microorganisms as a source of potential biological control agents aligns with sustainable agricultural strategies. This study is aimed at isolating, characterizing, and evaluating the in vitro antagonistic interactions, and antimicrobial potential of indigenous rhizospheric and endophytic bacteria with the potential...

item.title: Milk metabolomic signatures associated with naturally occurring Staphylococcus chromogenes subclinical mastitis in early-lactation dairy cows
item.description: CONCLUSION: Naturally occurring S. chromogenes subclinical mastitis was associated with exploratory alterations in the milk metabolome, particularly involving energy, amino acid, and fatty-acid metabolism. These durable responses indicate the potential to eliminate the need for current SOC and redefine the curative-intent treatment paradigm with dostarlimab in dMMR/MSI-H LARC.

item.title: Final prespecified analysis of the phase 3 LITESPARK-011 study: belzutifan plus lenvatinib versus cabozantinib for advanced renal cell carcinoma after anti-PD-(L)1 therapy
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Belzutifan plus lenvatinib continued to demonstrate PFS, ORR, and DOR benefit versus cabozantinib with additional follow-up; OS favored the combination but did not reach statistical significance at final analysis. Safety profile of belzutifan plus lenvatinib remained consistent with each drug as monotherapy. These findings continue to support belzutifan plus lenvatinib as a treatment option in advanced ccRCC following anti-PD-(L)1 therapy.

item.title: Integrated In Silico Discovery of the MMP9-Binding Phytochemicals from Ageratum conyzoides Using Molecular Docking, MD Simulation, and MM-GBSA Analysis
item.description: Matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP9) is a zinc-dependent endopeptidase, it remodels extracellular matrix and is implicated in chronic inflammation and cancer development. Despite their therapeutic potential, synthetic MMP inhibitors have poor selectivity and dose-limiting toxicities, highlighting the need for safer modulators. This study used a comprehensive in silico framework to identify MMP9-binding phytochemicals in Ageratum conyzoides. The IMPPAT database yielded 507 phytochemicals for...

item.title: Global carbon isotope variability of commercial plastics: implications for microplastic source attribution and environmental forensics
item.description: Microplastic source attribution remains a major challenge because conventional analytical techniques primarily identify polymer types while providing limited information on the origin and environmental history of plastic materials. This study evaluates the potential and limitations of stable carbon isotope analysis (δ^(13)C) for tracing common plastic polymers at the global scale. A total of 460 commercial plastic samples, including 233 polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles and 227...

item.title: Cytochalasin D-induced cytoskeletal remodeling with MYH9 enhances release of extracellular vesicles for therapeutic application
item.description: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) hold great potential as therapeutic vehicles, but their clinical application is limited by low production yields. Here, we explored whether the pharmacological disruption of the actin cytoskeleton using cytochalasin D (CytoD) could enhance EV release while maintaining properties essential for therapeutic use. We examined monocytic U937 cells and colorectal cancer SW480 cells, discovering that CytoD increased EV production by approximately 8.27-fold in U937 cells and...

item.title: Development of a photocaged CLIPTAC for spatiotemporal control of protein degradation
item.description: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) have emerged as a revolutionary therapeutic modality. However, their clinical translation is often hindered by high molecular weight, poor cellular permeability, and systemic off-target toxicity. To address these challenges, we report a photocaged click-assembled PROTAC (pcCLIPTAC) for the spatiotemporally controlled degradation of the BRD4 protein. Our system utilizes cycloalkene-based bioorthogonal handles and a light-sensitive photocaged...

item.title: The role of hope and its association with quality of life in individuals with chronic pain - insights from a daily diary study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Our daily diary study found that previous-day hope frequency - both stable individual differences and day-to-day fluctuations - was associated with next-day QoL in individuals with chronic pain who were co-using cannabis and opioids.

item.title: Prognostic associations between patient-reported outcomes and progression-free and overall survival in advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma with PD-L1 TAP score ≥ 5%: results from the RATIONALE-305 trial
item.description: CONCLUSION: PROs have significant prognostic value for disease progression and survival in patients with PD-L1 TAP score ≥ 5%.

item.title: Systemic and local delivery of siRNA to the CNS and periphery via anti-IGF1R antibody conjugation
item.description: siRNA delivery platforms capable of accessing both central and peripheral tissues are critically needed to expand the therapeutic potential of oligonucleotides. To address this, we developed an siRNA-antibody conjugate by attaching an Hprt-targeting siRNA to an engineered antibody shuttle. This shuttle targets the insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor (IGF1R) using a fused antibody fragment (Clone F) and utilizes an antibody backbone with no tissue-relevant binding in this study. The resulting...

item.title: Mediation of physical activity and sedentary behavior on the relationship between neighborhood greenness and cardiovascular outcomes
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These cross-sectional findings suggest that sedentary behaviour was consistently associated with the relationship between neighborhood greenness and cardiovascular outcomes. Place-making strategies that address sedentary behaviour may complement those that promote physical activity.

item.title: CDS-BART: a BART-based foundation model for mRNA sequence analysis
item.description: SUMMARY: Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have led to the development of foundation models that interpret mRNA as a language. Notable examples include CodonBERT, HydraRNA, Evo 2, and Helix-mRNA. These models demonstrate significant potential as powerful tools for mRNA research. However, to the best of our knowledge, there is currently no publicly available AI model that is both easy to use and capable of analysing mRNA sequences up to about 4 kb, a length scale typical of many...

item.title: A systematic approach to quantitative nanoscale mass spectrometry using atomic force microscopy
item.description: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) enables mass sensing through resonance-frequency changes of microcantilevers, but quantitative measurements can be affected by calibration and environmental factors. Here, we investigated whether a calibrated AFM cantilever and controlled mass loading could provide nanogram-scale mass estimation. Cantilevers were cleaned and calibrated by force-distance measurements, and resonance acquisition parameters were optimized under ambient conditions. UV-curable resin...

item.title: Treatment patterns and safety outcomes after splenectomy or thrombopoietin receptor agonists as second-line therapy for immune thrombocytopenia: Korean claims-based study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Patients treated with TPO-RAs as a second-line therapy showed a longer TTNT after 24 months, whereas VTE occurred earlier in the TPO-RA group. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution because of residual confounding.

item.title: Ancient somatosensory circuit architectures employ flexible molecular strategies
item.description: The extent to which conserved neural circuit architectures depend on shared molecular specification programs remains unclear. Here, we address this question by examining the somatosensory system of the little skate, Leucoraja erinacea, an early-diverging vertebrate that retains ancestral features of both finned and limb-based body plans. We show that core features of somatosensory circuit organization, including laminar organization of the spinal cord and dorsally restricted targeting of sensory...

item.title: Knowledge-guided taxon selection aligns eDNA with morphology-based diatom indices
item.description: Water quality assessment of rivers still depends on benthic diatom indices. In these schemes, microscopists enumerate living cells and combine the counts with published sensitivity values to produce a score that maps onto a legal water-quality class. The calculation itself is transparent, but the identification step does not scale readily as taxonomic expertise declines. Environmental DNA metabarcoding can supply a community inventory with far less specialist labor. Read counts, however, are a...

item.title: Five-Year Changes in Nurses' Compassion Competence and Associated Factors: A Longitudinal Study Using Explainable Machine Learning
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Nurses' compassion competence increased modestly over 5 years, supporting its conceptualization as a dynamic professional competency. Nursing work environment features were the most prominent, but exploratory, model-based contributors.
